events.title: Alaric II issues the Breviary of Alaric
events.description: The Visigothic king promulgated a digest of Roman law for the Roman population of his kingdom in Gaul and Spain. It became one of the main channels through which Roman law reached early medieval western Europe.
events.html: The Visigothic king promulgated a digest of Roman law for the Roman population of his kingdom in Gaul and Spain. It became one of the main channels through which Roman law reached early medieval western Europe.

events.title: Pedro de Mendoza founds Buenos Aires
events.description: The Spanish expedition founded a settlement on the Río de la Plata. Hunger and attacks forced its abandonment in 1541, and Juan de Garay refounded Buenos Aires in 1580.
events.html: The Spanish expedition founded a settlement on the Río de la Plata. Hunger and attacks forced its abandonment in 1541, and Juan de Garay refounded Buenos Aires in 1580.

events.title: New Amsterdam receives municipal government
events.description: The Dutch settlement on Manhattan was granted its own city government under Director-General Peter Stuyvesant. The English seized it in 1664 and renamed it New York.
events.html: The Dutch settlement on Manhattan was granted its own city government under Director-General Peter Stuyvesant. The English seized it in 1664 and renamed it New York.

events.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends the Mexican-American War
events.description: Mexico ceded about half its territory, including California, Nevada, Utah and most of Arizona and New Mexico, to the United States for 15 million dollars, and recognised Texas as American.
events.html: Mexico ceded about half its territory, including California, Nevada, Utah and most of Arizona and New Mexico, to the United States for 15 million dollars, and recognised Texas as American.

events.title: German Sixth Army's last units surrender at Stalingrad
events.description: The final German forces in Stalingrad's northern pocket laid down their arms. Some 91,000 were taken prisoner, and the defeat marked a turning point of the war on the Eastern Front.
events.html: The final German forces in Stalingrad's northern pocket laid down their arms. Some 91,000 were taken prisoner, and the defeat marked a turning point of the war on the Eastern Front.

events.title: Idi Amin proclaims himself President of Uganda
events.description: A week after his coup, Amin declared himself head of state and suspended parts of the constitution. His rule became one of the most brutal in post-colonial Africa until his overthrow in 1979.
events.html: A week after his coup, Amin declared himself head of state and suspended parts of the constitution. His rule became one of the most brutal in post-colonial Africa until his overthrow in 1979.

events.title: F. W. de Klerk lifts the ban on the ANC
events.description: Opening parliament in Cape Town, South Africa's President legalised the African National Congress and other banned groups and announced Nelson Mandela's release. Negotiations to end apartheid followed.
events.html: Opening parliament in Cape Town, South Africa's President legalised the African National Congress and other banned groups and announced Nelson Mandela's release. Negotiations to end apartheid followed.

events.title: IPCC finds global warming is 'very likely' caused by humans
events.description: Released in Paris, the summary of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's fourth assessment called warming 'unequivocal' and very likely due to human emissions. The panel shared that year's Nobel Peace Prize.
